item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem:
The graph shows the time of travel by pupils from home to school.

[Image: Graph showing time of travel by pupils from home to school]

How many pupils must travel for MORE than 10 minutes?

A bar graph with a vertical axis labeled "Number of Pupils" having tick marks numbered 1 through 10. The horizontal axis is labeled "Time (in minutes)" and shows four intervals:
- "0-5": bar height is 2
- "6-10": bar height is 7
- "11-15": bar height is 5
- "16-20": bar height is 2

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph represents the distance and time of a hike taken by Joshua and Liam.

[Image: Line graph of distance versus time]

If they both started from the same place and walked in the same direction, at what time did they meet?
reference_items.figure_description:
A line graph with a vertical axis labeled "Distance (kilometers)" marked from 0 to 5.5 in increments of 0.5 (labeled 0, 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, 3.0, 3.5, 4.0, 4.5, 5.0, 5.5). The horizontal axis is labeled "Time" with tick marks every 30 minutes from 8:00 to 12:30 (labeled 8:00, 8:30, 9:00, 9:30, 10:00, 10:30, 11:00, 11:30, 12:00, 12:30). Two line segments are shown:
- One labeled "Joshua" begins at (8:00, 0) and ends with a solid dot at (12:00, 4.5).
- One labeled "Liam" begins at (9:00, 0) and ends with a solid dot at (11:00, 4.5).
The two lines intersect at time 10:00 and distance approximately 2.25 kilometers.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Four students watched the traffic passing their school for 1 hour.

The table shows what they saw:

| Type of Vehicle | Number |
| :--- | :---: |
| Cars | 60 |
| Bicycles | 30 |
| Buses | 10 |
| Trucks | 20 |

Each student drew a graph to show the results. Which graph shows the results correctly?
reference_items.figure_description:
Four graphical representations of the traffic data:
- Option A: A vertical bar graph with the vertical axis labeled from 0 to 60 in increments of 10. The bars correspond to: Cars = 60 (solid black bar), Bicycles = 30 (light gray bar), Buses = 10 (medium gray bar), Trucks = 20 (white bar with black border).
- Option B: A pictograph with a legend stating '1 wheel = 10 vehicles'. Cars has 5 wheels, Bicycles has 4 wheels, Buses has 1 wheel, and Trucks has 2 wheels.
- Option C: A vertical bar graph with the same axis and colors as Option A, showing: Cars = 60, Bicycles = 30, Buses = 20, Trucks = 10.
- Option D: A pie chart divided into four sectors: Cars covers the right half (180°, solid black). Bicycles covers the bottom-left quadrant (90°, light gray). The remaining top-left quadrant is divided between Buses (a larger sector, medium gray) and Trucks (a smaller sector, white).
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.stem:
Triathlon

A triathlon is a race in which athletes swim, then cycle, then run set distances. The first person to complete the whole course is the winner.

Kathy, Barbara, and Sue competed with each other in a triathalon. The course they covered consisted of a 1 kilometer swim, followed by a 40 kilometer cycle ride, and then a 15 kilometer run.

C. Sue was the fastest runner. She averaged 7.5 km per hour for the 15 km run. Barbara took 10 minutes more than Sue, and Kathy took 5 minutes more than Barbara.

A beaker of water which has reached boiling point is allowed to cool. The temperature of the water is recorded at five minute intervals, and a temperature-time graph is drawn.

Cooling Curve

About how many minutes did it take for the water to cool the first 20 degrees?

The vertical axis is labeled "Temperature (°C)" with grid lines and numerical labels from 20 to 100 in increments of 20 (20, 40, 60, 80, 100), with 0 at the origin. The horizontal axis is labeled "Time (minutes)" with grid lines and numerical labels from 0 to 50 in increments of 5 (0, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50). A smooth curve starts at (0, 100) and decreases monotonically toward the right, passing through approximately (5, 74), (10, 55), (15, 43), (20, 37), (25, 32), (30, 28), (35, 24), (40, 22), (45, 21), and ending at (50, 20).

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The graph shows the distribution of crops grown in a certain country.

[Image: Pie chart showing the distribution of crops]

According to the information in the graph, which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: More oats are grown than wheat.

options.label: B
options.text: Corn is more than one-half of the country’s crop.

options.label: C
options.text: Oats are more than one-third of the country’s crop.

options.label: D
options.text: The total crop of oats and wheat is greater than the corn crop.

reference_items.figure_description:
A pie chart showing four sectors labeled with crop types:
- 'Corn': occupies slightly less than half of the circle, spanning from the 12 o'clock position clockwise to approximately the 4:30 position (roughly 135° to 140°).
- 'Oats': adjacent clockwise from Corn, spanning from approximately 4:30 to 7 o'clock (roughly 75°).
- 'Other': adjacent clockwise from Oats, spanning from approximately 7 o'clock to 8 o'clock (roughly 30°).
- 'Wheat': adjacent clockwise from Other to Corn, spanning from approximately 8 o'clock to 12 o'clock (roughly 115° to 120°).

The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration.
